reason: The cited evidence (E1–E3) directly supports all key premises: E1 states the ductility loss phenomenon and proposes principal-element segregation as the mechanism; E2 confirms the segregation of Cr, Mn, Ni and links it to ductility loss; E3 provides direct APT evidence of Cr, Ni, Mn enrichment at GBs and notes the absence of impurity segregation. The evidence is accurately represented and specific to the equiatomic Cr-Mn-Fe-Co-Ni system.
premises: Single-phase FCC Cr-Mn-Fe-Co-Ni alloys lose ductility at intermediate temperatures (400–800°C)
Ductility loss is accompanied by grain-boundary cracking and reduced strain hardening
Principal elements (Cr, Mn, Ni) segregate to grain boundaries during short-term tensile testing
This segregation causes grain-boundary decohesion and embrittlement
Preexisting precipitates can mitigate the segregation and restore ductility
